title: Wiener Schnitzel
subtitle: Viennese breaded veal escalope
excerpt: The Viennese classic: a very thin veal escalope, coated in fine breadcrumbs and fried in clarified butter until golden and puffed, served with a wedge of lemon and nothing else. Simplicity at the highest level.

recipe.sourceNotes: Wiener Schnitzel (Viennese schnitzel) is one of Austria's national dishes and a protected geographical indication: to be called Wiener Schnitzel, the cutlet must be veal, not pork. The dish is made from a very thin slice of veal (topside or cushion), pounded to about 4 mm, coated in a classic three-stage breading of flour, beaten egg, and fine dry breadcrumbs, and fried in clarified butter (or a mixture of butter and oil). The defining characteristic is the soufflé-like puffing of the breadcrumb coating during frying, which occurs when the fat is the right temperature and the crumbs have been applied loosely. The schnitzel should not be pressed after crumbing; the loose crumbs trap steam and puff away from the meat. Schnitzel served with lemon only is the authentic Viennese style.

content.text: Do not press the crumbs onto the meat; shake off any excess at each stage. Pressed crumbs fry into a hard, flat crust. Loose crumbs puff away from the meat and give the right texture. The fat must come halfway up the meat. Each side needs only 2 to 3 minutes.

items.preparation: cut into 2 escalopes of about 150 g each; pounded to 4 mm between cling film

content.text: Set up three shallow dishes: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs. Dip each escalope in flour (shaking off the excess), then egg (letting the excess drip off), then breadcrumbs (coating loosely without pressing). Do not press the crumbs at any stage.

Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan to about 170°C. The fat should come to at least 1 cm depth. Fry the schnitzels for 2 to 3 minutes per side, tilting the pan to baste the top with hot fat, until golden and puffed.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper. Serve at once with lemon wedges. Good sides include potato salad, cucumber salad, or lingonberry jam.
